raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview When a multi-turn conversation exceeds the server's context limit, `vllm chat` currently exits on an uncaught `BadRequestError`. Add opt-in `--interactive` (`-i`) so users can keep the full error diagnostics, clear history, and continue without restarting the client. ## Claims - Local `/help`, `/clear`, and `/exit` commands; `/clear` preserves the configured system prompt. `//` sends a literal leading slash. - Request and stream API errors print their full tracebacks and return to the prompt. Completed conversation history is preserved; failed or interrupted turns are explicitly not saved. Unexpected programming errors still propagate. - Optional `vllm[chat]` provides arrow-key history and Ctrl+A/B/E/F line editing through `prompt_toolkit`. Input history stays in memory, survives `/clear`, and is never written to disk. Piped input and missing optional dependencies fall back to plain input. - Existing fail-fast behavior remains the default. `--interactive` cannot be combined with `--quick`; SDK retries and model generation parameters are unchanged. ## Validation | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Client/SDK tests on macOS arm64, Python 3.12 | 11 passed | | Same client tests on Ubuntu, Python 3.10 | 11 passed; no GPU inference involved | | Real vLLM server context-overflow tests on macOS | 2 passed, covering both flag spellings | | Changed-file pre-commit hooks | Passed, including formatting, mypy, and CI test tethering | | Optional extra packaging | Built and verified `prompt-toolkit` in `vllm[chat]` metadata | | Actual macOS terminal | Edited `/hep` into `/help` with Ctrl+B; recalled history and exited cleanly | Commands run from the checkout: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_openai_cli.py -q PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion.py -k chat_cli -q .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/entrypoints/cli/openai.py \ tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_openai_cli.py \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion.py \ docs/cli/README.md setup.py .buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml ``` The client tests use the real `ChatCommand`, OpenAI SDK, and `PromptSession`, with an external HTTP fixture and actual editing key sequences. They cover HTTP 400, existing SDK retries on HTTP 500, interrupted streams, history preservation, local commands, literal slash escaping, missing editor fallback, and clean exits. They do not mock vLLM model state. The Linux run used a separate test/editor environment and the existing SDK dependencies with the same changed CLI source module. Real-model tests use `RemoteOpenAIServer` and SmolLM2-135M-Instruct weights with a 512-token limit. macOS validation used vLLM Metal and precompiled vLLM 0.32.0 CPU artifacts with the source checkout. The new tests are selected by the existing Entrypoints Unit and OpenAI chat_completion CI steps; the unit step installs the optional editor. No Windows runtime was available. `prompt_toolkit` supports Windows terminals and Unix-only signal registration is guarded, but this does not add or claim native Windows vLLM engine support. No serving/model computation changes, model-quality improvements, or performance gains are claimed. ## Details ### Original failure and recovery The CLI sends accumulated conversation history on every request. A long assistant answer can therefore make the next short user message exceed the configured context limit. Only EOF was caught in the input loop; the API error escaped and terminated the client. The following excerpts shorten the pasted prompt and traceback for readability. The actual client prints the full SDK exception and traceback in both modes. Before, with a server configured for 512 tokens: ```text $ vllm chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 Using model: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct Please enter a message for the chat model: > ["hello " repeated 600 times] Traceback (most recent call last): ... openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - ... This model's maximum context length is 512 tokens. However, your prompt contains at least 513 input tokens ... $ # Client exited with status 1; /clear cannot be entered. ``` After, with opt-in interactive mode: ```text $ vllm chat -i --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 Using model: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct Please enter a message for the chat model: Commands: /help, /clear, /exit. Prefix a message with // to send /. > ["hello " repeated 600 times] Traceback (most recent call last): ... openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - ... This model's maximum context length is 512 tokens. However, your prompt contains at least 513 input tokens ... Request failed or response was interrupted; this turn was not saved. Previous conversation is unchanged. Use /clear to start over or enter another message. > /clear Conversation cleared; system prompt preserved. > /help Commands: /help, /clear, /exit. Use // to send a leading /. > /exit $ # Clean exit with status 0. ``` The live base-commit reproduction exited 1 on HTTP 400 before it could process `/clear`. With `-i`, the changed code printed the same diagnostic, processed `/clear`, successfully served another request, and exited 0 with `/exit`. Separately, the new real-key regression test failed against pre-editor commit `1e5ae0c` and passed after the editor change. To reproduce an overflow, start a server with a small context limit: ```bash vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --max-model-len 512 \ --max-num-seqs 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.1 --enforce-eager ``` In a second terminal, run the following once without `-i` and once with it: ```bash .venv/bin/python -c 'print("hello " * 600); print("/clear"); print("/help"); print("/exit")' \ | vllm chat -i --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 ``` This scripted reproduction tests error recovery and local commands. To use line editing in a terminal, install `uv pip install 'vllm[chat]'` and run `vllm chat -i` without piping stdin/stdout. ### Scope and tradeoffs The two existing chat loops are consolidated through the existing `chat` function. A new turn enters conversation history only after a complete successful response; partial output stays visible but is explicitly excluded from subsequent requests. Startup/model-discovery failures and unexpected programming exceptions remain fail-fast. The line editor is lazily enabled only for `-i` with terminal stdin and stdout. Keyboard history is separate from the model's conversation history, so `/clear` can recover context space without losing input recall. The mode does not add retries, silently truncate history, compact/summarize conversations, or increase the server context limit. Duplicate-work checks on 2026-10-24 found no overlapping open PR using targeted searches for `"vllm chat" in:title`, `"CLI" "error" in:title`, `"chat" "interactive" in:title`, `"chat" "readline"`, and `"chat" "prompt_toolkit"`. The Rust chat-types refactor (#49576) concerns server protocol types, not this client loop. No existing issue is claimed as fixed. AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation, tests, documentation, and this description. The validation results above were run by Codex; the human author directed the design and approved preparing this contribution. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

@@ -35,7 +35,9 @@ steps:
   - tests/entrypoints/unit_tests
   - tests/entrypoints/launchers

+  - uv pip install --system 'prompt-toolkit>=3.0.52,<4'

@@ -98,8 +98,40 @@ vllm chat --quick "hi"
 
 # Print TTFT and throughput statistics after each response
 vllm chat --stats
+
+# Enable chat commands and recover from API errors
+vllm chat --interactive
 ```
 
+`--interactive` (alias `-i`) is opt-in and cannot be combined with `--quick`. It enables
+`/help`, `/clear` (reset conversation history while preserving the configured
+system prompt), and `/exit`. Commands are handled locally; prefix a message with
+`//` to send a literal leading slash. Unknown commands display a hint without
+sending a request.
+
+Install the optional line editor with `uv pip install 'vllm[chat]'`. In `-i` mode,
+when both input and output are terminals, it enables arrow-key input history and
+Emacs-style editing (Ctrl+A/Ctrl+E for the start/end of the line and
+Ctrl+B/Ctrl+F for moving backward/forward). The line editor uses `prompt_toolkit`,
+which supports Linux, macOS, and Windows terminals; it does not change vLLM's
+platform requirements. Without this optional dependency, or when input/output
+is redirected, the CLI uses plain `input()`.
+
+Input history stays in memory for the current chat session and is not written to
+disk. It is separate from the conversation sent to the model: `/clear` resets
+the conversation but keeps recalled input available through the arrow keys.
+Ctrl+C and end-of-input exit the prompt cleanly.
+
+In this mode, API errors during a chat request or response stream print their
+full traceback and return to the prompt. Startup errors still propagate.
+Previously completed turns remain in history; a failed or interrupted turn is
+not saved, even if part of its answer was already printed. The client does not
+automatically retry interrupted streams, truncate history, or summarize it.
+The OpenAI SDK's existing request retries are unchanged. Use `/clear` to recover
+when a conversation exceeds the server's context limit. Unexpected programming
+errors still propagate. Without `--interactive`, slash-prefixed messages are
+sent to the model and API errors propagate as before.
+
 See [vllm chat](./chat.md) for the full reference of all available arguments.
 
 ## complete

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import argparse
+import io
+import json
+import queue
+import sys
+import threading
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
+
+import openai
+import pytest
+from prompt_toolkit.application import create_app_session
+from prompt_toolkit.input import create_pipe_input
+from prompt_toolkit.output import DummyOutput
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.cli.openai import ChatCommand
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def chat_api():
+    """Only the external model service is replaced; use the real CLI and SDK."""
+
+    class RequestLog(list):
+        def __init__(self):
+            super().__init__()
+            self.received: queue.Queue[dict] = queue.Queue()
+
+        def append(self, item):
+            super().append(item)
+            self.received.put(item)
+
+    requests = RequestLog()
+    failures: dict[str, int | str] = {}
+
+    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+        def log_message(self, *args):
+            pass
+
+        def respond(self, status, body, content_type="application/json"):
+            self.send_response(status)
+            self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
+            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
+            self.send_header("Retry-After", "0.001")
+            self.end_headers()
+            self.wfile.write(body)
+
+        def do_GET(self):
+            self.respond(200, b'{"data":[{"id":"test-model"}]}')
+
+        def do_POST(self):
+            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
+            requests.append(body)
+            failure = failures.get(body["messages"][-1]["content"])
+            if isinstance(failure, int):
+                self.respond(
+                    failure,
+                    b'{"error":{"message":"diagnostic details","type":"test_error"}}',
+                )
+                return
+            chunk = {
+                "id": "test",
+                "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
+                "created": 0,
+                "model": "test-model",
+                "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"content": "reply"}}],
+            }
+            payload = "data: " + json.dumps(chunk) + "\n\n"
+            if failure == "stream":
+                payload += 'data: {"error":{"message":"stream interrupted"}}\n\n'
+            else:
+                payload += "data: [DONE]\n\n"
+            self.respond(200, payload.encode(), "text/event-stream")
+
+    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
+    thread.start()
+    try:
+        yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/v1", requests, failures
+    finally:
+        server.shutdown()
+        server.server_close()
+        thread.join()
+
+
+def run_chat(monkeypatch, url, text, *flags):
+    parser = ChatCommand.add_cli_args(argparse.ArgumentParser())
+    args = parser.parse_args(["--url", url, *flags])
+    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", io.StringIO(text))
+    ChatCommand.cmd(args)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("flag", ["-i", "--interactive"])
+def test_commands_clear_history_but_preserve_system_prompt(
+    chat_api, monkeypatch, capsys, flag
+):
+    url, requests, _ = chat_api
+    run_chat(
+        monkeypatch,
+        url,
+        "/help\n/unknown\n\nfirst\n/clear\n//literal\n/exit\n",
+        flag,
+        "--system-prompt",
+        "Be concise.",
+    )
+    assert len(requests) == 2
+    assert requests[-1]["messages"] == [
+        {"role": "system", "content": "Be concise."},
+        {"role": "user", "content": "/literal"},
+    ]
+    output = capsys.readouterr().out
+    assert "Unknown command" in output
+    assert "Conversation cleared" in output
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure,attempts", [(400, 1), (500, 3), ("stream", 1)])
+def test_api_errors_keep_completed_history_and_full_diagnostics(
+    chat_api, monkeypatch, capsys, failure, attempts
+):
+    url, requests, failures = chat_api
+    failures["reject"] = failure
+    run_chat(monkeypatch, url, "first\nreject\ncontinue\n/exit\n", "-i")
+    assert len(requests) == attempts + 2
+    assert requests[-1]["messages"] == [
+        {"role": "user", "content": "first"},
+        {"role": "assistant", "content": "reply"},
+        {"role": "user", "content": "continue"},
+    ]
+    error = capsys.readouterr().err
+    assert "Traceback" in error
+    assert "Previous conversation is unchanged" in error
+    assert (
+        "stream interrupted" in error
+        if failure == "stream"
+        else (f"Error code: {failure}" in error and "diagnostic details" in error)
+    )
+
+
+def test_default_mode_preserves_literal_commands_and_propagates_errors(
+    chat_api, monkeypatch, capsys
+):
+    url, requests, failures = chat_api
+    failures["reject"] = 400
+    with pytest.raises(openai.BadRequestError, match="diagnostic details"):
+        run_chat(monkeypatch, url, "/clear\nreject\n")
+    assert requests[0]["messages"] == [{"role": "user", "content": "/clear"}]
+    assert "Conversation cleared" not in capsys.readouterr().out
+
+
+def test_interactive_rejects_quick_mode(capsys):
+    parser = ChatCommand.add_cli_args(argparse.ArgumentParser())
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):

+def test_terminal_line_editing_and_history_survive_conversation_clear(
+    chat_api, monkeypatch, exit_keys
+):
+    """Feed real editing keys through a real PromptSession, without a display."""
+    url, requests, _ = chat_api
+    cleared = threading.Event()
+
+    class Terminal(io.StringIO):
+        def isatty(self):
+            return True
+
+        def write(self, text):
+            result = super().write(text)
+            if "Conversation cleared" in text:
+                cleared.set()
+            return result
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", Terminal("fallback\n/exit\n"))
+    output = Terminal()
+    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdout", output)

+    args = parser.parse_args(["--url", url, "-i", "--system-prompt", "Be concise."])

+    with (

+        create_app_session(input=keys, output=DummyOutput()),
+    ):
+        errors: list[Exception] = []
+
+        def type_messages():
+            try:
+                keys.send_text("alpha\n")
+                assert (

+                    == "alpha"
+                )
+                keys.send_text("\x1b[A\x01\x06\x02X\x05\x02Y\n")
+                assert (
+                    requests.received.get(timeout=10)["messages"][-1]["content"]
+                    == "XalphYa"
+                )
+                keys.send_text("/clear\n")
+                assert cleared.wait(timeout=10)
+                keys.send_text("\x1b[A\x1b[A\x1b[A\x1b[B\n")
+                requests.received.get(timeout=10)
+                keys.send_text(exit_keys)
+            except Exception as error:
+                errors.append(error)
+                keys.send_text("\x04")
+
+        driver = threading.Thread(target=type_messages)
+        driver.start()
+        ChatCommand.cmd(args)
+        driver.join(timeout=15)
+        assert not driver.is_alive()
+        assert not errors
+
+    assert len(requests) == 3
+    assert requests[0]["messages"][-1]["content"] == "alpha"
+    assert requests[1]["messages"][-1]["content"] == "XalphYa"
+    assert requests[2]["messages"] == [
+        {"role": "system", "content": "Be concise."},
+        {"role": "user", "content": "XalphYa"},
+    ]
+    assert "Conversation cleared" in output.getvalue()
